correctness.rationale: Independent support of an iDRDF on R_mn is a partial row/column matching with no 1-labels (a 1 would require a positive neighbor contrary to independence). Every zero requires a positive neighbor, forcing matching to saturate all m rows. When square, each zero sees one supported neighbor in each direction and exactly 2s suffice, giving weight 2m and m! permutation optima. When m<n, an unoccupied column gives one-positive-neighbor zero per row, forcing all supported 3s and weight 3m with n!/(n−m)! injections. The argument covers m,n≥2. Independently checked all four-label assignments on R_2,2, R_2,3, R_2,4 and R_3,3 (the largest 4^9 cases), with exact minima and optimizer counts; no extrapolation from these finite checks.

evidence: General same-parameter theory proves lower/upper bounds; for square m=n, i(R)=m and every zero of an independent 2-dominating permutation matrix has two support neighbours.
For m<n an empty column forces label3 at each supported row; this equality classification is not an automatic consequence of general weight bounds.

value.rationale: Rectangular rook graphs are standard Cartesian products/line graphs. The sharp square-versus-nonsquare transition is forced by board geometry and gives complete algebraic families of every optimal labeling, bijectively permutations or injections. This is an exact structured classification beyond an isolated score; the pre-known square bound alone does not determine the strict rectangular phase or all optimizers.

final_claim: For 2≤m≤n, i_dR(K_m □ K_n)=2m when m=n and 3m otherwise, with all minimum labelings bijective to n! permutation 2-labelings in square case and n!/(n−m)! injection 3-labelings otherwise.
limitations: The square scalar follows established general bounds together with independent 2-domination geometry; only all-optimizer and rectangular phase are differentiated.
